correctness.rationale: The monomial coefficient formula and integral pair potential hold for every alpha>0. Differentiation proves strict convexity and the exact endpoint slopes, including divergence at alpha<=2. Weighted chord-variance identity and supporting tangents prove global sufficiency and uniqueness even at equality; mass-balanced angular splitting gives the exact negative quadratic variation below threshold. Infinite endpoint slope excludes all collisions at alpha<=2 by a balanced group displacement or an oriented one-pole displacement. Verification checker independently confirms symbolic alpha=3 coefficient, Fourier-integral equivalence and representative energies; universal proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary manuscripts were compared by mathematical statements. The equal-residue weighted Bergman optimality theorems, the arbitrary-positive-charge L1 field lower bound, and indexed literature about equal-pole local Hessians do not cover the sharp heavy/light mass-only all-antipode threshold. Eleven actual semantic searches returned no same statement; this is conditional, not proof of historical uniqueness. One broad preprint and published indexed full texts remain uninspected, recorded as residual risks.

value.rationale: Unequal charge extension of a newly revisited sharp weighted Bergman pole-placement problem has a previously unquantified structural phase transition: whether an entire positive-residue population can stably collapse at an antipode is governed only by its total mass, not its cardinality or distribution. The sharp global threshold and alpha=2 collision regularity boundary distinguish repulsion from heavy charge confinement, and supply motivated extremal configurations and quantitative gaps useful in weighted Chui problems.
